prompt: What balance metadata (heights, colors, balance factors, etc.) does a Splay Tree store per node?
explanation: Splay trees keep no balance metadata at all — structure comes purely from rotations triggered by access (splaying).

prompt: Splay Tree delete: the target is found and splayed to the root. The root's left subtree L is non-empty. What single node from L becomes the new root, and why does attaching R to it require no further checks?
acceptedAnswers: the maximum of L, because it has no right child
the largest node in L, it has no right child
maximum of L has no right child
explanation: The maximum of L is splayed to become L's new root; being the maximum, it has no right child by definition, so R attaches directly into that free slot.

prompt: [Lecture example] Starting from the tree rooted at 12 (right child 20, whose children are 13 and 21, with 13's right child 15), insert 14, 18, 17, 11, 16, 19 in that order. What is the value at the root of the final tree?
explanation: Splay insert always finishes by splaying the just-inserted node to the root — so after inserting 19 last, 19 is the root, regardless of the intervening rotations.

prompt: [Lecture example] Continuing from the tree built in the previous question, search for 15, then delete 18. What is the value at the root of the final tree?
explanation: Deleting 18 first splays it to the root (via find), removes it (splitting into L and R), then splays the maximum of L to become the new root before attaching R — which lands on 17 for this tree.
